jobDescription: Lumenfold sells booking software to clinics, salons and fitness studios, and its notifications platform sends confirmations and reminders by email, SMS and push. The Backend Engineer writes and maintains Go services on that platform, designs the queue consumers that carry retries, instruments services so that faults can be traced, and joins the on-call rota after onboarding. Every change reaches customers through a gated release pipeline with an approval step, and engineers watch their own releases in live operation. Engineers review each other's merge requests and hand open alerts over at a weekly meeting.
requirements: Builds and maintains backend services in Go with automated tests that run on every merge.
Designs message-queue consumers with retry limits and dead-letter handling.
Has released backend changes to production through a gated release pipeline and supported them in live operation.
Instruments services with structured logs and metrics and uses them to diagnose faults.
Reviews colleagues' merge requests and takes part in the weekly alert handover.

evidence.text: Software Engineer on the developer-tooling squad at Tessera Cloud, April 2022 to July 2024. Wrote and maintained three Go services behind an outbound webhook relay, with table-driven unit tests and contract tests that ran in the CI pipeline on every merge request.
Designed the relay's queue consumer with exponential backoff, a cap of eight delivery attempts and a dead-letter topic that support staff could browse and replay from.
Deployed the relay to the shared staging cluster and load-tested it at up to 2,000 messages per second; the platform team held the release pipeline and any onward rollout.
Reviewed merge requests for two other engineers on the squad and drafted a code-review checklist that the squad adopted in 2023.

Instrumented the relay with structured logs and per-endpoint request metrics, used them to trace a duplicate-delivery fault during the staging load tests, and presented open staging alerts at the squad's weekly handover.

Work sample: a runbook titled 'Webhook relay - sandbox namespace', explaining how to start the relay in the sandbox, rotate the test signing key and replay messages from the dead-letter topic. Each page header reads 'Environment: sandbox'. The closing section, headed 'Go-live', contains a single line: 'Relay went live on 22 May for the four internal test tenants (qa-01 to qa-04).'

HR verification note: the employment dates (April 2022 to July 2024) and the job title Software Engineer were checked against a reference letter that Tessera Cloud's people team sent to us directly; both match the resume.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate has a four-week notice period and asked whether on-call weeks carry a standby allowance.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote and maintained three Go services with unit and contract tests that ran in CI on every merge request.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry states the services and the tests that ran in the CI pipeline.

propositions.text: The candidate deployed the webhook relay to a shared staging cluster and load-tested it at up to 2,000 messages per second.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the deployment and the load tests on the staging cluster and says the platform team held the release pipeline.

propositions.text: The candidate released the webhook relay to production and supported it in live operation from 22 May.
propositions.rationale: The only go-live wording sits in a runbook whose pages are all marked 'Environment: sandbox' and whose go-live line names internal test tenants; the resume says the platform team held the release pipeline. The deployment rule forbids describing sandbox work as a production release or live operation when no source says it ran in production.

gold.expectedGap: The relay's deployment is documented only on the staging cluster and in a sandbox namespace; no production release or live-operation duty is documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the Go services, the retry consumer, the instrumentation and the staging load tests as written; describe the runbook as a sandbox runbook and keep its go-live line tied to the internal test tenants.
followUpTargets: Ask which environments the relay ran in while the candidate was at Tessera Cloud, who approved and executed any production release, and whether the candidate had run-time or on-call responsibility for it.
